value_stream.name: Global Mobility, Immigration & Foreign Worker Compliance

fields.Owner: Head of Global Mobility / HR Strategy
fields.Participants: CHRO (VS-19), CFO/Controller (VS-17), Tax (VS-79), Legal (VS-100.3), Chief Security Officer (VS-159), Strategy (VS-33)
fields.Trigger: Talent/business strategy (VS-33); new foreign-hire need; annual review

workflows.name: Global Mobility Strategy, Policy & Assignment-Tax Framework

Automation Opportunity: - Policy/handbook portal; assignment-intake workflow; tax-treaty decision support
Controls: - CTL-710 (ensure controlled execution — Mobility Strategy, Policy & Assignment Framework (PA-160.1).)
- CTL-710: mobility policy CHRO/CFO-endorsed; assignment-tax framework Tax-led (VS-79); assignments initiated via policy intake
Cross-references: - links to VS-33 (strategy), VS-79 (tax), VS-100.3 (legal), VS-123 (local-talent development), VS-159 (security), W4714 (assignment tax)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Ad-hoc-assignment risk**: Assignments handled case-by-case without policy → inconsistent packages, tax errors, and inequity; mitigated by the documented policy
- **Tax-treaty-misapplication risk**: Mis-applied treaty/19-series withholding → tax exposure and employee cost; mitigated by Tax-led framework (VS-79)

steps.activity: Define the global-mobility strategy and policy aligned to talent and business strategy (VS-33): when to deploy foreign expertise vs. develop local talent (VS-123 apprenticeship), the assignment-tax framework, and the governance with Legal/Tax/Chief Security Officer (VS-159)
steps.r: Head of Global Mobility / CHRO / Tax

steps.activity: Set assignment-tax principles: residency determination (resident vs. non-resident), tax-treaty application, 19-series withholding for non-residents, tax-equalization vs. tax-protection, and home/host split (W4714)
steps.r: Head of Global Mobility / Tax / Legal

steps.activity: Obtain leadership endorsement; publish the mobility policy and assignment handbook; train HR/business leaders on when/how to initiate an assignment (intake to W4702)

fields.Participants: HR Business Partners (VS-19/VS-103), Tax (VS-79), Immigration (PA-160.2), hiring managers
fields.Volume: ~20–40 assignments/year across types (foreign executives, seconded experts, provincial transfers)

workflows.name: Assignment Types: Long-Term, Short-Term, Commuter, Localization & Business-Visitor Policy

Automation Opportunity: - Assignment-classification decision tool; per-type package templates; assignment-letter generation
Controls: - CTL-710 (ensure controlled execution — Mobility Strategy, Policy & Assignment Framework (PA-160.1).)
- CTL-710: classification framework applied; business-visitor vs. work-permit line enforced; genuine-business-need documented
Cross-references: - links to W4702 (records), PA-160.2 (immigration), W4713/W4714 (payroll/tax), W4716 (housing), VS-98 (contingent-workforce distinction)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mis-classification risk**: A long-term assignment run as a business-visitor/commuter → immigration/tax violation; mitigated by the classification framework and Legal review
- **Labor-only-contracting-confusion risk**: A foreign "assignee" structure that masks labor-only-contracting (VS-98/DOLE D.O. 174); mitigated by the genuine-business-need test

steps.activity: Classify each assignment by type — long-term (LT, typically >12 months, with relocation/family), short-term (ST, <12 months, no family relocation), commuter (regular cross-border without relocation), localization (permanent host-country conversion), and business-visitor (short meetings, no work-permit) — each with distinct immigration/tax/payroll treatment

Apply the per-type package and compliance (immigration W4705–W4707, payroll/tax W4713/W4714, housing W4716, duty-of-care W4704) and confirm the assignment meets the policy test (genuine business need, not labor-only-contracting avoidance VS-98)

steps.a: Head of Global Mobility / VP Legal
steps.activity: Document the assignment decision and terms in the assignment letter; ensure the business-visitor vs. work-permit line is not crossed (visitor doing productive work = immigration violation)

fields.Owner: Head of Global Mobility / Finance Partner

workflows.name: Mobility Cost-Budget, Package Design & Balance-Sheet vs. Lump-Sum

Automation Opportunity: - Assignment-costing calculator; package templates; actual-vs-budget dashboards
Controls: - CTL-710 (ensure controlled execution — Mobility Strategy, Policy & Assignment Framework (PA-160.1).)
- CTL-710: assignment cost per policy and approval matrix; actual-vs-budget tracked; localization reviewed
Cross-references: - links to VS-17.4 (FP&A), VS-102 (comp), VS-72 (entity), W4716 (housing), W4718 (localization), W4720 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cost-creep risk**: Uncapped assignment allowances inflate cost; mitigated by the package policy and approval matrix
- **Over-expatriation risk**: Expatriate assignments continued when localization would be cheaper/better (VS-123); mitigated by localization review (W4718)
System Touchpoints: - Finance/FP&A (VS-17.4); comp (VS-102); HR (VS-19); procurement (VS-34); mobility analytics (W4720)

steps.activity: Cost each assignment: base salary, assignment allowances (premium, hardship, cost-of-living differential), housing (VS-144/W4716), relocation, tax-equalization cost, schooling (dependents), and return trips; choose balance-sheet (maintain home-country spend + host differentials) vs. lump-sum (VS-102)
Build the annual mobility budget (by entity VS-72); approve assignments per the cost-approval matrix (tiered by cost); track actual vs. budget
Identify cost-optimization (localization W4718 vs. continued expatriation, package benchmarking VS-102) and report mobility spend analytics (W4720)

fields.Volume: ~6–10 mobility vendors (immigration agents, relocation firms, tax-equalization providers, assignment-payroll vendors)

Automation Opportunity: - Vendor SLA dashboards; TPRM integration (VS-161); PII-handling attestation tracking
Controls: - CTL-710: vendors TPRM-vetted (VS-161); SLA-managed; PII protected (VS-91); conduct assured (VS-86)
Cross-references: - links to VS-34/VS-161 (procurement/TPRM), VS-67 (scorecard), VS-91 (privacy), VS-86 (ABC)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vendor-failure risk**: An immigration agent's error causing visa denial/overstay → compliance exposure; mitigated by TPRM (VS-161) and SLA
- **PII-breach risk**: Assignee PII (passport, family, health) breached by a vendor; mitigated by data-protection agreements (VS-91)
System Touchpoints: - Procurement/vendor (VS-34); TPRM (VS-161); vendor scorecard (VS-67); contracts (VS-100.3); privacy (VS-91)

steps.activity: Select and contract mobility vendors (immigration agents, relocation firms, tax-equalization/assignment-payroll providers) via procurement (VS-34) and TPRM due diligence (VS-161): licensure, data-security (assignee PII VS-91), conflicts

Govern vendor performance (immigration success rate, relocation SLA, payroll accuracy); manage the lifecycle (renewal/exit VS-67/VS-161); enforce data-protection agreements (assignee data is sensitive PII VS-91)

steps.a: Head of Global Mobility / VP Legal
steps.activity: Assure vendor conduct (no corruption in immigration processing VS-86); manage sole-source justification for specialized services

fields.Owner: Head of Global Mobility / HR Operations
fields.Participants: Store Ops (VS-07), Talent (VS-121/VS-103), HRBP, Comp (VS-102), Employee Accommodation (VS-144)
fields.Trigger: Domestic transfer/promotion (VS-19); new-store-opening staffing (VS-37); 10–15 new stores/yr

workflows.name: Domestic Mobility, Transfers & Provincial Relocation Program

Automation Opportunity: - Transfer/relocation workflow; regional cost-differential calculator; transfer-success analytics
Controls: - CTL-710 (ensure controlled execution — Mobility Strategy, Policy & Assignment Framework (PA-160.1).)
- CTL-710: transfer package per comp policy (VS-102); relocation/accommodation coordinated; transfer success tracked
Cross-references: - links to VS-19/VS-103 (HR/talent), VS-102 (comp), VS-144 (accommodation), VS-37 (store opening), VS-159 (duty-of-care)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Transfer-failure risk**: A failed transfer (family/adjustment) → turnover and cost; mitigated by relocation support and accommodation (VS-144)
- **Pay-parity-error risk**: Regional pay-differential mis-applied → inequity or cost; mitigated by the comp framework (VS-102)
System Touchpoints: - HR/HRIS (VS-19/VS-103); comp (VS-102); accommodation (VS-144); store ops (VS-07); store opening (VS-37)

steps.activity: Manage domestic transfers and provincial relocations: transfer-need identification, candidate selection (VS-19/VS-103), relocation package (regional cost differential VS-102), and family/relocation support

Coordinate relocation logistics (moving, housing VS-144, school, spousal-support info), regional pay differential and statutory continuity (SSS/PhilHealth/Pag-IBIG are national), and duty-of-care for high-risk provincial postings (VS-159)
Track transfer success (retention, performance) and feed lessons into the talent and new-store-opening (VS-37) staffing model; manage transfer failure/return

Automation Opportunity: - Assignment-record system integrated with HRIS/payroll/immigration; lifecycle-event automation; PII access controls
Controls: - CTL-710 (ensure controlled execution — Mobility Strategy, Policy & Assignment Framework (PA-160.1).)
- CTL-710: assignment data integrated and PII-governed (VS-91); lifecycle events fed to dependent systems; retained per policy (VS-88)
Cross-references: - links to VS-103/VS-27 (HRIS), VS-29 (master data), VS-91/VS-88 (privacy/records), VS-79 (tax)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Data-silo risk**: Assignment data in spreadsheets not integrated with HRIS/payroll/immigration → errors; mitigated by the integrated assignment-record system
- **PII-breach risk**: Assignee/dependent PII exposed; mitigated by sensitive-PII governance (VS-91)
System Touchpoints: - HRIS (VS-103/VS-27); master data (VS-29); payroll/tax (VS-19.2/VS-79); records (VS-88); privacy (VS-91)

steps.activity: Maintain the assignment-record system: assignment data (type, home/host entity, dates, package, immigration status, tax status, dependents, housing) integrated with HRIS (VS-19/VS-103) and master data (VS-29); govern as sensitive PII (VS-91)
Administer the assignment lifecycle events in the system: start, mid-assignment changes, extensions, localization (W4718), and end/repatriation (W4718); feed payroll/tax/immigration systems
Assure data quality and retention (VS-88); provide assignment data to Tax (VS-79), audit (VS-21), and immigration compliance (W4711) on need

fields.Participants: Compliance (VS-22), Legal (VS-100.3), Tax (VS-79), Chief Security Officer (VS-159), Internal Audit (VS-21)
fields.Trigger: Risk review; compliance-calendar event; KPI reporting

workflows.name: Mobility Risk, Compliance Calendar & KPI Framework

Automation Opportunity: - Compliance-calendar with automated renewal alerts; KRI dashboards; ERM integration
Controls: - CTL-710: compliance calendar maintained with alerts; mobility KRIs in ERM; program assured via VS-21/VS-22
Pain Points / Risks: - **Overstay/lapse risk**: A visa/I-Card lapsing unnoticed → overstay (BI penalty, deportation, officer liability); mitigated by the compliance calendar with automated alerts
- **KRI-blind risk**: Mobility risks not surfaced in ERM; mitigated by KRI integration (VS-21.2)
System Touchpoints: - Compliance calendar; assignment-record (W4702); ERM (VS-21.2); compliance (VS-22); audit (VS-21)

steps.a: Head of Global Mobility / VP Legal
steps.activity: Operate the mobility compliance calendar: AEP/visa/I-Card renewals (W4705/W4706), tax filings (W4714), statutory remittances (W4715), and BI/DOLE audit-readiness; automated renewal alerts
Maintain mobility KRIs (visa-overstay incidents, renewal-late events, tax-error rate, assignment cost, localization rate, transfer retention); report to HR leadership and integrate with ERM (VS-21.2)

steps.a: Head of Global Mobility / VP Legal
steps.activity: Manage mobility-risk events (overstay, audit, incident) and assure the program via Internal Audit (VS-21) and compliance (VS-22)

fields.Owner: Head of Global Mobility (joint with the Chief Security Officer (VS-159))

fields.Volume: ~15–25 foreign assignees traveling to/from PH (per W4705); sourcing secondees per VS-122

Automation Opportunity: - Assignee-traveler-tracking enrollment; joint mobility-security workflow; event-triggered activation
Controls: - CTL-710: cross-border assignees briefed + tracked (VS-159); duty-of-care discharged; joint response on event
Cross-references: - links to VS-159 (corporate security/travel risk), W4679/W4687/W4688 (destination risk/tracking), VS-83 (OH)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Duty-of-care gap risk**: An assignee in a high-risk location without security/travel-risk support → harm and liability; mitigated by VS-159 linkage
- **Coordination-gap risk**: Mobility and security not coordinated → blind traveler; mitigated by joint protocol
System Touchpoints: - Traveler-tracking (VS-159 W4687); destination-risk (VS-159 W4679); OH (VS-83); assignment-record (W4702)

steps.a: Head of Global Mobility / Chief Security Officer
steps.activity: For each cross-border assignee, coordinate with Corporate Security (VS-159) on travel-risk briefing, destination-risk intelligence (VS-159 W4679), and duty-of-care during assignment travel
steps.r: Global Mobility / Chief Security Officer / Travel Risk

steps.a: Head of Global Mobility / Chief Security Officer
steps.activity: Ensure assignees are enrolled in traveler-tracking and emergency protocols (VS-159 W4687/W4688); coordinate medical-evacuation and security support for high-risk locations
steps.r: Global Mobility / Chief Security Officer / OH

steps.a: Head of Global Mobility / Chief Security Officer
steps.activity: On a security/travel-risk event affecting an assignee, activate the VS-159 response and support the assignee/family; feed lessons into mobility-risk (W4703)
